Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 43 (Digital Realty missing-address campaign): added a multi-source agreed address, reconciled the Tempe versus Phoenix market page labeling as normal metro grouping rather than a conflict.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, a Digital Realty facility in Tempe, AZ, matches a datacenterHawk listing and independent DataCenterJournal coverage both giving 2055 East Technology Circle, Tempe, AZ. The operators own market page groups this facility under its broader Phoenix market heading, consistent with this registrys website field, even though the specific city is Tempe.

reading.body:
This Tempe facility, operated by Digital Realty at 2055 East Technology Circle, is confirmed in location and operator but lacks published power specifications for its individual buildings. The data provided does not include megawatt capacity, critical IT load, or rack count for this site, making it impossible to translate its physical scale into accelerator density or training capability.

Within Arizona's mapped data center footprint of 56 facilities, only 4 have published power figures totaling 512 MW of capacity statewide. This campus ranks fifth among Arizona's published capacity facilities, but without its own published specification, its actual power draw and contribution to that ranking cannot be determined from operator disclosure alone.

The research status is complete for location and operator identity. Whether this facility matters to AI scaling depends on figures not yet published in the operator's spec pages—total power, IT load allocation, and cooling delivery. Until those specifications appear, the site's role in the grid constraint on AI infrastructure remains unmeasured.
